recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision changes HumanName.given cardinality or the display/search guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-5533 asked whether HumanName.given and HumanName.family should be simple strings rather than repeated strings because repeated name parts could be interpreted as alternate combinations. It was Published/Persuasive with Modification; the approved disposition was to clarify that repeated given/family parts are parts of one name, explain the relationship between text and parts, and emphasize HumanName.text.
initial_application: Jira records that the HumanName narrative was updated in svn revision 4613. Git commit 998d6fc99991c1662bcf15c1d675a92a99683741, '#5533 - human name clarifications', changed source/datatypes.html to add the requested guidance about name parts, alternate HumanName instances, culture-dependent assembly, text for presentation, and parts for search/indexing.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini marks HumanName as a normative current datatype, and current source/datatypes.html still contains the substance of the FHIR-5533 resolution. source/datatypes/humanname.xml now has HumanName.family as 0..1 string and HumanName.given as 0..* string. The later Published core issue FHIR-12351 deliberately changed family-name cardinality and added decomposition guidance/extensions, refining the family-name model without reversing the FHIR-5533 clarification. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-5533-specific community discussion or conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The combined branch received an empty audit commit documenting that the current build-scope HumanName source is already correct for FHIR-5533.
